what_it_does: HBM (High-Bandwidth Memory) is a type of RAM that sits right on top of or beside an AI chip and is connected through thousands of tiny vertical wires (called through-silicon vias, or TSVs) punched through stacked silicon layers — think of a multi-story building of memory. HBM is excellent at reading data sequentially, but its speed for random, scattered reads — the kind needed for graph processing, recommendation systems, or AI models with irregular data access — has barely improved across generations. Folded Banks (FB-HBM) redesigns the internal layout of HBM by redistributing the storage subarrays across multiple layers and adding a new dedicated control layer at the base. This shortens the internal electrical paths that carry data between storage cells and sense amplifiers (the circuits that detect stored bit values), reducing the energy wasted as heat and increasing the bandwidth available for random accesses.
